solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Force chaps to infiltrate second corporation

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside something, so one piece slips within another

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time
chaps are men
a corporation is a jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A takeover story: a gang of men forced into a company to steal its seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' in the old sense of a pot belly is a crossword favourite; 'Force' looks like police but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and in sport, momentum is the driving impetus of a moving body, a kind of force.

clue.text: A new hotline must be organised at once

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to set up a new emergency phone line immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail means paying immediately, so the idiom means at once.

clue.text: Set aside steel to be carried by European vessel

indicators.note: what is carried is held inside the carrier, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
steel is a sword, a weapon or arm
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Steel cargo put aside to be shipped on a European boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel as a poetic word for a blade, and so a weapon, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to reserve them for a purpose, setting them aside.

clue.text: Route Greek cartographer crosses on way north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards
the letters cross the gap between two words, spanning them

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An ancient mapmaker's road crossing the land as he heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards, greeK CARTographer gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a path or way, so it is a route.

clue.text: Force offering amnesty from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters; the same letters also run across two later clue words, a coincidence

explanation.surface: A police force occasionally granting a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A police force is a force, and the Met is London's.

clue.text: Advocate coppers should have jurisdiction

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p
a jurisdiction is the reach or extent of authority

explanation.surface: A lawyer's demand that the police be given power over a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' and 'coppers' suggest lawyers and police, but coppers here are coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to urge it publicly, as a preacher urges a creed.

clue.text: Do peers ever stick to their guns?

indicators.note: a do is a party or a swindle, and as a verb to do something is to work it over, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether members of the House of Lords ever hold firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as the auxiliary starting a question, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite opposition, which is what sticking to your guns means.

clue.text: Call English knight "señor" in Spain?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
N is the knight in chess notation
señor is the Spanish form of address, an example of a title

explanation.surface: Wondering how to address an English knight while he is in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book is to call it by a name.

clue.text: Papers read out loud for those singing

indicators.note: reading out loud means we hear the word rather than see its spelling

parts.note: a quire is a set of sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Sheet music read aloud for the singers.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a measure of paper, twenty-four or twenty-five sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of singers performing together.

clue.text: Disturbance in the Scrubs perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a commotion or fuss
second meaning: slang for prison, of which Wormwood Scrubs is an example

explanation.surface: A report of trouble breaking out inside a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs, 'the Scrubs', is a London prison; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commotion and, in slang, a jail, and the Scrubs is one such jail.

clue.text: A change in how much beer you drink? About time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drinking phrase wraps round the extra letter

parts.note: ale is beer
T is the abbreviation for time
a ration is the measured amount you are allowed

explanation.surface: A drinker told it is high time to cut back on the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' sounds like an exasperated cheer, but 'About' is the container signal wrapping the letter for time.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is a modification, so it is simply a change.

clue.text: Embark with earl after travelling? That's odd

indicators.note: after travelling the letters have been moved about and arrive jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Surprise that a nobleman would set sail after he has already been travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odd is unusual and so worth remarking on: the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Less of a shock for one leaving here?

definitions.text: Less of a shock for one leaving here?

parts.note: surface reading: a smaller fright or surprise

parts.words: Less of a shock for one leaving here?
parts.note: setter's reading: a shock of hair is reduced for each customer walking out of these shops

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' means a mass of hair; the place you leave with less of it is where hair is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbers' shops are where men's hair is trimmed, so customers leave with a smaller shock.

clue.text: End of transition leaving you undecided?

wordplay.note: the word transition starts and finishes with the same choice of letters

explanation.surface: A change that ends with you unable to choose.
explanation.walkthrough: Transition begins with T and ends with N, so whichever end you pick, it is T OR N, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn describes someone pulled between two choices and unable to decide.

clue.text: Secret instruction that makes you cross

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as an order, it says back the word door, giving rood, a cross

explanation.surface: A covert order that leaves someone annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a clue-within-a-clue: BACK DOOR tells you to write DOOR backwards, which gives ROOD, an old word for a cross or crucifix. 'Cross' looks like 'angry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A back-door arrangement is one made covertly, so the phrase as an adjective means secret.

clue.text: Musical dramas back to back, merging in effect

indicators.note: merging means the two share a letter where they meet, so one copy is removed

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the second show is read in reverse

parts.note: Evita is a stage musical by Lloyd Webber and Rice

explanation.surface: Two musical shows staged one after the other, blending together.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA forwards then EVITA backwards, overlapping on the shared A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that is operative is in force, so it is in effect.

clue.text: Released, being old and almost completely useless

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ex means former, old
something empty is hollow and of no use

explanation.surface: Someone let go from work for being past it and good for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means freed or released from an obligation.

clue.text: Ban for wielder of a quill?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a scribe writes by hand, traditionally with a quill pen

explanation.surface: A question whether anyone still using a quill pen should be banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a scribe might use another pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid it, to ban it.

clue.text: Classmate ultimately failing to pass

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a lapse is a failing or slip

explanation.surface: A schoolmate who, in the end, did not pass the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to pass' reads as flunking a test; 'to pass' is the definition, in the sense of time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or slips by.

clue.text: Fixed payment sees writers hit back

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the chart term is read in reverse

parts.note: a hit record is a No. 1, written NO I

explanation.surface: A regular wage that sees writers strike back.
explanation.walkthrough: A chart hit is a 'number one', written NO 1 with the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a regular fixed sum paid to someone after retirement.

clue.text: English banker getting axed — or estate manager?

parts.note: a banker is a river, and the Exe is an English river in Devon
axed means cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A financier losing his job, or perhaps a property manager doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, something with banks; here it is the Exe.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor carries out a will and administers the dead person's estate.

clue.text: Vulnerable Cockney's safe and sound

indicators.note: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: safe and sound means uninjured

explanation.surface: A vulnerable Londoner who is nevertheless safe and well.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which drops H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons one is defenceless, so unarmed means vulnerable.

clue.text: This might make painter tell a tale

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fibre twisted into rope, and a painter is a boat's mooring rope
second meaning: to spin a long story

explanation.surface: Something that might set an artist storytelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' here is not an artist but the rope used to tie up a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is spun fibre used in rope-making, and as a verb it means to tell a long tale.

clue.text: A sub reportedly abandoned

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan of money

explanation.surface: A submarine said to have been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' suggests a submarine or substitute; here it is money advanced, a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abandoned is left by themselves, alone.

clue.text: MI6 in a position to provide support

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the spy service sits inside the posture

parts.note: a stance is a position
MI6 is the Secret Intelligence Service, the SIS

explanation.surface: Britain's spy agency positioned to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: SIS goes inside A STANCE, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is help given, the same thing as support.

clue.text: Cracking crime coming first in mountain region

indicators.note: coming first means placed at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime
A1 means first-rate, cracking, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Solving a crime that happened first in some mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like breaking into something; it is the adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the mountainous Egyptian peninsula, home to Mount Sinai.

clue.text: Implication millions lost — terrible for the Chancellor, say

indicators.note: terrible suggests a mess, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lost means gone missing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A news line: millions lost, a disaster for the finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from IMPLICATION and rearrange the rest. The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK's finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor is a senior government minister, an example of a politician, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Spike half cut, the rogue

indicators.note: half cut means half of it is chopped off, so only the first half stays

parts.note: to spike is to impale

explanation.surface: A drunk rogue skewered: 'half cut' is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous rascal, so a rogue in the playful sense.

clue.text: Hurt overthrowing most of city

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn upside down, so the letters run the other way
most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Miami is a city in Florida

explanation.surface: Injuries caused when a city's government was toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: To maim is to injure severely, so it is to hurt.

clue.text: Spiteful chap that is stalking Norm

indicators.note: stalking means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: the mean is the norm or average
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A nasty man shadowing someone called Norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name but means average.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is an informal word for an unkind, spiteful person.

clue.text: Troubled Euripides endlessly praying here?

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Greek tragic playwright

explanation.surface: A troubled Greek dramatist forever at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S from Euripides and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk where a person prays, so it is a place for praying; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
